title: the Crescent Cove Rising
premise: Cellist Sebastian Sterling retreats to Crescent Cove to sell her late grandmother's seaside inn, treating her shattered performing career like a muscle to be trained back into submission. While packing the attic she finds an unsent letter from her grandmother, postmarked eleven years earlier, revealing a lost love and a bequest contingent on someone 'staying after the last train leaves.' The letter's addressee turns out to be Jonah Reyes, the inn's quiet caretaker — and the man Sebastian once loved and abandoned. As the inn's fate and the last seasonal train converge, Sebastian must choose between the controlled life she rebuilt and the inheritance of memory her grandmother left her; the story ends with her staying past the last train, reopening the inn, and playing again — not for an audience, but for the people she loves.
about_author: August Lockridge is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who traded concert halls for coastal towns and now writes love stories about second chances and the things we inherit. The author lives in a renovated lighthouse keeper's cottage with a rescue dog and a stubborn piano.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. After a catastrophic final concert, she arrives at Crescent Cove to sell her grandmother's inn, armed with checklists and emotional distance. The caretaker, Jonah, greets her without surprise, and she flinches at the familiarity. Beat: guarded arrival; the reader senses the town knows her better than she admits.

chapters.title: Dust and D Major
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Packing the inn, she finds her grandmother's cello and can't resist playing; Jonah overhears from the doorway. A brittle exchange reveals shared history neither will name. Beat: the past intrudes through music; Sebastian's containment strategy shows its first cracks.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In the attic she discovers an unsent, yellowed letter from her grandmother, postmark older than her death, addressed to someone in the Cove. Its opening lines hint at a hidden bequest: the inn goes only to whoever 'stays after the last train leaves.' Beat: inciting mystery; grief becomes curiosity.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We learn Jonah has kept the inn running for eleven years, unpaid beyond room and board, waiting for something he won't explain. He recognizes Sebastian instantly and has rehearsed indifference for a decade. Beat: his devotion reframes every earlier scene; tension of withheld truth.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following the letter's clues to the boathouse, she finds her grandmother's old correspondence — a decade-long love with a man who left on the last train of the season and never came back. She realizes the letter's addressee is still nearby. Beat: inheritance as pattern; she fears repeating it.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Platform
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the station's centenary festival, Jonah and Sebastian nearly confess — he that he was the boy her grandmother loved's son and the letter's intended recipient; she that she left him eleven years ago without a word. An old rival developer interrupts with a purchase offer. Beat: rising stakes; the inn's sale now threatens the letter's promise.

chapters.title: The Muscle Remembers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Cornered by the offer and her own fear, Sebastian plays the cello at the festival hall and freezes mid-piece — until she stops performing and plays for the room. Jonah is in the back row. Beat: midpoint climax of her internal arc; vulnerability chosen, not forced.

chapters.title: Eleven Winters
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah finally tells her everything: her grandmother wrote to him the winter Sebastian disappeared, asking him to wait for her granddaughter instead. He never opened the letter until now. Beat: emotional climax of the romance; betrayal and tenderness collide.

chapters.title: The Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. On the final night of the season, with the sale papers signed and a taxi to the station ordered, Sebastian stands on the platform as the train arrives. The letter's condition echoes in her head. She lets it go without her. Beat: climax; the choice that fulfills the inheritance.

chapters.title: Staying After
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, then Sebastian's. Spring returns: the inn reopens under both their names, the grandmother's letter finally framed above the hearth. Sebastian books no concerts but plays Sunday nights in the parlor for whoever stays. Beat: resolution; belonging, memory, and inheritance braided into a home rather than an ending.
